{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Implement the increment as Java-based Mule modules following existing Mule extension, lifecycle, configuration, and DeploymentService conventions.",
    "Use the existing Mule domain model so a domain can contain multiple applications and domain lifecycle operations propagate to all associated applications.",
    "Expose domain deploy, undeploy, and redeploy operations through the Mule deployment API, with redeploy performing application updates after the domain is available.",
    "Implement application-property overrides as deployment-time values supplied to DeploymentService, with deployment values taking precedence over packaged defaults without modifying the application archive.",
    "Define the AMQP configuration and message processor syntax using the project's supported Mule XML schema and namespace conventions so IDE validation and autocompletion are available.",
    "Provide a reusable global AMQP transport configuration for common connection, authentication, acknowledgment, and connection-management attributes.",
    "Use a standard AMQP client library already compatible with the target Mule runtime, isolating broker-specific behavior behind the transport connector abstraction.",
    "Implement continuous consumption as a source that listens to a queue, converts each received AMQP message into a MuleEvent, and dispatches it to a flow.",
    "Implement instant consumption as an inbound message processor that performs a receive operation at the point where it appears in a flow.",
    "Use configurable acknowledgment behavior, connection recovery, timeout handling, and error propagation consistent with existing Mule transport patterns.",
    "Add unit tests, deployment lifecycle tests, schema validation tests, and broker-backed integration tests for the supported AMQP consumption modes."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The increment extends an existing Mule codebase with standard build, test, deployment, and extension frameworks already available.",
    "Existing DeploymentService APIs and domain/application lifecycle abstractions can be extended rather than implemented from scratch.",
    "A compatible AMQP broker, such as RabbitMQ, is available for integration testing, and broker provisioning is limited to test configuration.",
    "AMQP support is limited to queue consumption for this increment; publishing, exchanges, routing-key management, and advanced transaction coordination are out of scope unless required by existing framework contracts.",
    "The supported AMQP protocol and client-library versions are selected by the existing project baseline and do not require a new broker protocol implementation.",
    "Deployment-time property overrides are key-value properties and do not require a new secrets-management system.",
    "Backward compatibility is required for existing domain deployment, application deployment, and transport configuration behavior.",
    "The base project skeleton includes agreed package structure, extension metadata, configuration placeholders, lifecycle hooks, endpoint or connector placeholders, transaction extension points, and example tests.",
    "Specification review work consists of documenting the implementation specification, acceptance criteria, examples, and contribution feedback mechanism; it does not include product management or external community moderation.",
    "Code review, local defect correction, and normal build troubleshooting are included in the activity estimates.",
    "Estimates represent individual software development effort in work-hours and exclude elapsed waiting time for external approvals or infrastructure provisioning."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Requirements analysis and technical design",
      "activity_description": "Analyze U1-U8, map the requirements to Mule runtime extension points, define lifecycle behavior, AMQP message semantics, configuration precedence, error handling, and acceptance criteria.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Specification review and contribution material",
      "activity_description": "Prepare reviewable technical specifications, configuration examples, terminology, open design points, and feedback-oriented documentation for product owners and community contributors.",
      "most_likely_effort": 12
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Base project skeleton",
      "activity_description": "Create or update the project modules, package structure, build metadata, extension descriptors, lifecycle interfaces, connector and endpoint placeholders, transaction extension points, and initial test scaffolding.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "AMQP XML schema and metadata",
      "activity_description": "Define the AMQP namespace, XSD elements and attributes, global configuration syntax, continuous and instant consumption elements, validation rules, metadata, and IDE-oriented documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Reusable global AMQP transport configuration",
      "activity_description": "Implement a single reusable AMQP configuration point covering broker connection settings, credentials, virtual host, queue defaults, acknowledgment behavior, timeouts, connection recovery, and shared client resources.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Domain deployment lifecycle",
      "activity_description": "Implement and integrate domain deploy, undeploy, and redeploy operations, including discovery of domain applications, lifecycle ordering, propagation of failures, cleanup, and application updates during redeployment.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Application deployment with property overrides",
      "activity_description": "Extend DeploymentService integration to accept deployment-time application properties, resolve precedence against packaged and default properties, apply values during startup, and expose appropriate validation and errors.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Continuous AMQP message consumption",
      "activity_description": "Implement queue listener startup and shutdown, message reception, AMQP-to-MuleEvent conversion, flow dispatch, acknowledgment handling, concurrency configuration, reconnect behavior, and listener error handling.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Instant AMQP message consumption",
      "activity_description": "Implement an in-flow receive operation that consumes a message on demand, supports queue and timeout configuration, converts the result into the expected Mule message or event representation, and handles empty or failed receives.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Unit, schema, lifecycle, and integration testing",
      "activity_description": "Create automated tests for schema validation, configuration resolution, property precedence, domain lifecycle operations, AMQP event conversion, acknowledgment and reconnect behavior, continuous consumption, instant consumption, and failure scenarios using a test broker.",
      "most_likely_effort": 52
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "User documentation and examples",
      "activity_description": "Document deployment APIs, property overrides, domain lifecycle usage, AMQP global configuration, continuous and instant consumption, configuration reference, examples, limitations, and troubleshooting guidance.",
      "most_likely_effort": 20
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A12",
      "activity_name": "Integration, packaging, and release readiness",
      "activity_description": "Integrate modules, resolve compatibility issues, run the complete build and regression suite, verify generated artifacts and schemas, update versioned metadata, and prepare the increment for delivery.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 400
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment as Java-based Mule modules following existing Mule extension, lifecycle, configuration, and DeploymentService conventions.
Use the existing Mule domain model so a domain can contain multiple applications and domain lifecycle operations propagate to all associated applications.
Expose domain deploy, undeploy, and redeploy operations through the Mule deployment API, with redeploy performing application updates after the domain is available.

Implement application-property overrides as deployment-time values supplied to DeploymentService, with deployment values taking precedence over packaged defaults without modifying the application archive.
Define the AMQP configuration and message processor syntax using the project's supported Mule XML schema and namespace conventions so IDE validation and autocompletion are available.
Provide a reusable global AMQP transport configuration for common connection, authentication, acknowledgment, and connection-management attributes.
Use a standard AMQP client library already compatible with the target Mule runtime, isolating broker-specific behavior behind the transport connector abstraction.
Implement continuous consumption as a source that listens to a queue, converts each received AMQP message into a MuleEvent, and dispatches it to a flow.
Implement instant consumption as an inbound message processor that performs a receive operation at the point where it appears in a flow.
Use configurable acknowledgment behavior, connection recovery, timeout handling, and error propagation consistent with existing Mule transport patterns.
Add unit tests, deployment lifecycle tests, schema validation tests, and broker-backed integration tests for the supported AMQP consumption modes.
assumptions: The increment extends an existing Mule codebase with standard build, test, deployment, and extension frameworks already available.
Existing DeploymentService APIs and domain/application lifecycle abstractions can be extended rather than implemented from scratch.
A compatible AMQP broker, such as RabbitMQ, is available for integration testing, and broker provisioning is limited to test configuration.

AMQP support is limited to queue consumption for this increment; publishing, exchanges, routing-key management, and advanced transaction coordination are out of scope unless required by existing framework contracts.
The supported AMQP protocol and client-library versions are selected by the existing project baseline and do not require a new broker protocol implementation.
Deployment-time property overrides are key-value properties and do not require a new secrets-management system.
Backward compatibility is required for existing domain deployment, application deployment, and transport configuration behavior.

The base project skeleton includes agreed package structure, extension metadata, configuration placeholders, lifecycle hooks, endpoint or connector placeholders, transaction extension points, and example tests.

Specification review work consists of documenting the implementation specification, acceptance criteria, examples, and contribution feedback mechanism; it does not include product management or external community moderation.
Code review, local defect correction, and normal build troubleshooting are included in the activity estimates.
Estimates represent individual software development effort in work-hours and exclude elapsed waiting time for external approvals or infrastructure provisioning.

activities.activity_description: Analyze U1-U8, map the requirements to Mule runtime extension points, define lifecycle behavior, AMQP message semantics, configuration precedence, error handling, and acceptance criteria.
Prepare reviewable technical specifications, configuration examples, terminology, open design points, and feedback-oriented documentation for product owners and community contributors.

Create or update the project modules, package structure, build metadata, extension descriptors, lifecycle interfaces, connector and endpoint placeholders, transaction extension points, and initial test scaffolding.
Define the AMQP namespace, XSD elements and attributes, global configuration syntax, continuous and instant consumption elements, validation rules, metadata, and IDE-oriented documentation.

Implement a single reusable AMQP configuration point covering broker connection settings, credentials, virtual host, queue defaults, acknowledgment behavior, timeouts, connection recovery, and shared client resources.

Implement and integrate domain deploy, undeploy, and redeploy operations, including discovery of domain applications, lifecycle ordering, propagation of failures, cleanup, and application updates during redeployment.

Extend DeploymentService integration to accept deployment-time application properties, resolve precedence against packaged and default properties, apply values during startup, and expose appropriate validation and errors.

Implement queue listener startup and shutdown, message reception, AMQP-to-MuleEvent conversion, flow dispatch, acknowledgment handling, concurrency configuration, reconnect behavior, and listener error handling.

Implement an in-flow receive operation that consumes a message on demand, supports queue and timeout configuration, converts the result into the expected Mule message or event representation, and handles empty or failed receives.

activities.activity_name: Unit, schema, lifecycle, and integration testing
activities.activity_description: Create automated tests for schema validation, configuration resolution, property precedence, domain lifecycle operations, AMQP event conversion, acknowledgment and reconnect behavior, continuous consumption, instant consumption, and failure scenarios using a test broker.

Document deployment APIs, property overrides, domain lifecycle usage, AMQP global configuration, continuous and instant consumption, configuration reference, examples, limitations, and troubleshooting guidance.

Integrate modules, resolve compatibility issues, run the complete build and regression suite, verify generated artifacts and schemas, update versioned metadata, and prepare the increment for delivery.
